** *
 Judgment

The petitioner has filed the claim petition U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 19.11.2015 at about 08.00 p.m, the petitioner after finishing his shooting work, return to his home in Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-04-EZ-9216 on NH-4 Express Highway, when he reached near Agarwal Hotel at Adakamaranahalli,
Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the Bus bearing No.KA-11-A-1134 stopped the bus on the middle of the road at night, the (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.831/2020 driver of the bus has not taken any precautionary measures, the driver of the bus negligently stopped the bus at the middle of the road, due to which the petitioner was dashed the bus from behind.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to HOSMAT hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient and he was under bedrest for 6 months and he has spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance,
nourishment and food.
At the time of accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and acting in serials and also doing agriculture and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
On account of the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his profession and agriculture, presently he is under treatment and now he is getting headache and giddiness.
The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Bus and in this regard the Madanayakanahalli Police have registered a case against driver of the offending Bus.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.831/2020 liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- to the petitioner together with cost and interest.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence, was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending Bus, age, income, occupation of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and denies existence of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Bus bearing No.KA-11-A-1134 and its validity since it is not been confirmed from the concerned policy issuing office.
If the owner of the vehicle were to produced original policy, the liability of this respondent is strictly in terms and conditions of the policy.

The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and contended that the respondent No.1 had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving (SCCH-3) 5

B. Rahamathulla Khan

on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27719522/
2 M.V.C.No.831/2020 to drive the same as on the date of accident and allowed to ply his vehicle on the road without having valid permit and it clear breach of terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of M.V. Act and the offending Bus is not involved in the accident and the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle by the petitioner himself and there was no negligence on the part of driver of the bus and compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and hence pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 19.11.2015 at about 08.00 p.m, on NH-4, near Agarwal Hotel,
Bengaluru Nelamangala Highway, Adakamaranahalli, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of the driving of the Bus bearing registration No.KA-11-A-1134 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove his case, the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and got examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Manager (Claims) as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.

09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In Affirmative  Issue No.2 In partly affirmative  Issue No.3
As per final order  for the following:
REASONS 10.
Issue No.1:- Petitioner filed affidavit as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments.

Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.831/2020 respondent No.2 Chetan.R vs B. Rahamathulla Khan on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27719522/
3 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Bus by its driver, the accident took place and petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

entities.text: (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.831/2020 respondent No.2 Chetan.R vs B. Rahamathulla Khan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Madanayakanahalli Police against driver of the offending Bus.

Ex.P.2 shows that the petitioner himself lodged the complaint after 12 days of accident stating that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Bus the accident was occurred and due to which he fell down and sustained injuries and he explained reasons for delay stating that he took treatment in HOSMAT hospital, Bengaluru and he sustained grievous injury to his leg, due to which he could not walk properly and after recovered he lodged belated complaint which was written by his father.
Ex.P.3 is the important document of Investigation Officer.
After completion of the investigation filed Charge sheet against driver of the offending Bus for the offences punishable U/s 279, 338 of IPC.

Ex.P.4 is Spot Mahazar showing the place of accident on NH-4 Express Highway, near Agarwal Hotel, Bengaluru Nelamangala Road, Adakamaranahalli, Bengaluru, (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.831/2020 which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is copy of IMV report which discloses that involvement of both vehicles in the accident and both vehicles are damaged.

Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which shows that the petitioner sustained closed fracture midshaft right femur and left elbow posteromedial dislocation with radial head fracture and said injury Nos.1 and 2 are grievous in nature.

Ex.P.7 and 8 are the Discharge summaries which shows that the petitioner sustained closed fracture midshaft right femur with left elbow posteromedial dislocation with radial head fracture and left radial head fracture (2 months old).
11.
To disprove the petitioner case, RW.1 filed affidavit and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the written statement averments.
During his cross-examination

he admits that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending bus was in force and denied to the suggestion that the accident occurred due to negligence of bus driver and the Charge sheet has been filed against bus driver and they have not challenged Charge sheet anywhere and he has produced copy of Policy at Ex.R.2 which shows that as on the date of accident the policy of the offending bus is valid and is in force.

The oral and (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.831/2020 documentary evidence produced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Bus and petitioner sustained injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and acting in serials and also doing agriculture and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and he has spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance, nourishment and food.
Due to accidental injuries, he became permanent disabled and sustained pain and sufferings, loss of income.

13. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate,
school records or SSLC marks card or Aadhaar card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he admits in his cross-examination that his date of birth is 26.06.1990 (SCCH-3) 10 Chetan.
R vs B. Rahamathulla Khan

on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27719522/
4 M.V.C.No.831/2020 and the alleged accident occurred on 19.11.2015.
Hence, it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner is 25 years.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 25 years and as per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is 18.
14.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With regard to avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2015 to be taken as Rs.9,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.9,000/-.
15.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained fracture dislocation left elbow (fracture of the radial head) and right femur shaft fracture and he assessed upper and lower limb (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.831/2020 disability at 58% and whole body disability at 20% and he has produced X-rays, Outpatient record and Inpatient record as per Ex.P.13 to 15.
In his cross- examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally.
Petitioner took treatment at Hosmat hospital.
The treated doctor has not issued the disability certificate.
As per recent x-ray the present condition of the petitioner fracture is united but left elbow is mal-united with deformity and arthritis.
For mal-union corrective surgery is not require but to reduce the pain we have do fusion.
On left elbow fracture and dislocation and further admits that range of movements in knee and ankle is normal.
Fracture taken place mid shaft of right femur and said fracture is united, there are no other complication.
There is no bone loss and limb shortening.

Implants on right lower limb is already removed and he has strictly followed the guidelines of Central Government notification and to considered whole body he has to take 1/3rd of the particular limb disability and no estimation given for future surgery and cost to be vary from hospital to hospital.

However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.831/2020 disability of the petitioner at 1/4th i.e., 14.5%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
 Rs.9,000/- x 12 x 18 x 14.5%/100 =
Rs.2,81,880/-.
16.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
The petitioner has produced Discharge summaries of HOSMAT hospital, Bengaluru, according to which he was admitted as inpatient twice in the said hospital only for 08 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

17. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and as per Inpatient medical records, Outpatient record and X-rays and on account of accidental injuries,
petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.831/2020 fractures suffered by him in the Chetan.R vs B. Rahamathulla Khan on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27719522/
5 accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
18. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.9,000/- p.m and he was admitted in the hospital for 08 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast two months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.18,000/-
(Rs.9,000 x 2) under this head.

19. Medical expenses:- The petitioner has produced entire Medical bills as per Ex.P.9 for Rs.22,896/- and inpatient final bill of Shirdi Sai hospital as per Ex.P.10 for Rs.54,750/-, totalling to Rs.77,646/-.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondent No.2 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.77,646/- under this head.
20. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.831/2020 grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
21. Future medical expenses:- According to doctor PW.2 the petitioner may need fussion for left elbow arthritis in future when the pain becomes unbearable, which will cost of Rs.1,50,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Hence, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.50,000/- under this head.
22. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 2,81,880-00  2. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00
3 . Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges
4. Medical Expenses 77,646-00  5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00  unhappiness  (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.831/2020  6. Loss of income during laid up 18,000-00  period  7.
Future medical expenses 50,000-00  Total 5,17,526-00 Chetan.R vs B. Rahamathulla Khan on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27719522/

6 23. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,17,526/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.50,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
24. Regarding liability:- Despite service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.
On service of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared and filed written statement and contest the matter, but despsite sufficient opportunity, they have not proved their contention by examining RW.1.
On the date of accident policy was in force as per Ex.R.2.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.

Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.831/2020 date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

25. Issue No.3:- In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,17,526/- (Rupees Five lakhs seventeen thousand five hundred and twenty six only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.50,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The petitioner is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on system, corrected, initialed and then pronounced by me in open court on 09th day of October, 2025).
(B.S.HONNASWAMY) VII Addl. Judge and ACJM, Bengaluru.
